findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Update the inline block comment in `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` (lines 424-432) to reflect that `--cov` flags are ubuntu-only after the conditional change (e.g. note 'ubuntu cells only: coverage is reported... macOS skips `--cov`').
evidence: Plan Scope: '_build-and-test.yml — the `test` job default-suite step only' — does not enumerate updating the inline comment
Workflow line 424: '# Coverage is reported (term-missing) and carries a conservative floor'
Workflow line 431: '# Coverage combines correctly only because `parallel = true` is set in [tool.coverage.run] (pyproject.toml).'
ABSENCE: no mention of updating or removing the comment block in the plan text
findings.finding: The inline block comment inside the default-suite step (`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` lines 424-432) states 'Coverage is reported (term-missing) and carries a conservative floor... Coverage combines correctly only because `parallel = true` is set in [tool.coverage.run]' — language that implies coverage runs on every matrix cell. After the proposed OS-conditional change this comment will be inaccurate for the macOS cell, yet the plan does not enumerate updating it.
findings.location: .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml, lines 424-432 (inline block comment in the default-suite step)
scenarios: A contributor reads the workflow after the change and sees the comment saying 'Coverage is reported' on the macOS cell step, which is no longer true — the comment becomes misleading documentation drift.
A future reviewer auditing the workflow for correctness will find the comment contradicts the actual conditional behavior.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace or augment the comment block so it says, e.g.: 'ubuntu cells: coverage is reported (term-missing) and carries a conservative floor (fail_under in [tool.coverage.report], pyproject.toml)... macOS cells omit --cov (coverage is collected on ubuntu only — see docs/coverage.md).'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a concrete in-session proving command for ACs #1 and #2 — e.g., a `yq` or `python -c` invocation against `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` that asserts the ubuntu step contains `--cov=rebar` and the macOS step does not, so the conditional is verifiable without triggering a live CI run.
evidence: '`tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` pins the substring `pytest -m "not integration and not external"` (line 67), which this change preserves'
AC #1: 'The macOS matrix cells run the default suite with no `--cov` or `--cov-report` flags.'
AC #2: 'The ubuntu matrix cells still pass `--cov=rebar --cov-report=term-missing:skip-covered`.'
ABSENCE: No grep, yq, or python command is given to assert the YAML conditional structure or to verify per-OS flag presence/absence in a CI log.
findings.finding: ACs #1 and #2 (the core behavioral change — macOS cells omit `--cov`; ubuntu cells retain it) have no concrete in-session proving command. The only named test (`test_ci_workflow_parity.py` line 67) pins the test-selection substring, not the `--cov` flag conditionality. No grep/yq/python command against the YAML structure is specified to verify the conditional is correctly wired for each matrix OS.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC #1, AC #2; Testing section
scenarios: An executor adds the wrong conditional (e.g., negated predicate) — ubuntu loses coverage, macOS keeps it — and no in-session command catches it before merge.
The YAML conditional is syntactically valid but logically inverted; `make lint` and `test_ci_workflow_parity.py` both pass green while the behavioral change is backwards.
findings.suggested_fix:
Add to the Testing section:
```
# Verify YAML structure in-session:
python -c "
import yaml, sys
wf = yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml'))
steps = {s['name']: s for job in wf['jobs'].values() for s in job.get('steps', [])}
# confirm ubuntu step contains --cov, macOS step does not
# (exact key paths depend on the conditional implementation chosen)
"
```
Or add an AC: `grep -E '\-\-cov=rebar' .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml | grep -v macos` exits 0, and `grep -E '\-\-cov=rebar' .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml | grep macos` exits 1.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend AC#7 to require that `docs/coverage.md` also documents *why* coverage is ubuntu-only (e.g. references the duplicate-work rationale and the macOS runner scarcity context), matching the Scope section's stated intent.
evidence: Scope: 'docs/coverage.md — record that coverage is collected on the ubuntu cells only, and why.'
AC#7: 'docs/coverage.md states that CI collects coverage on the ubuntu cells only.' — omits any verification of the rationale.
findings.finding: AC#7 only verifies the *what* of the docs/coverage.md update ('states that CI collects coverage on the ubuntu cells only'), but the Scope section describes the deliverable as 'record that coverage is collected on the ubuntu cells only, AND WHY.' An implementer verifying solely against AC#7 could write a one-line doc with no rationale and pass — the 'why' portion of the described deliverable has no covering criterion.
scenarios: Implementer writes a single sentence 'Coverage is collected on ubuntu cells only.' in docs/coverage.md, passes AC#7, but the rationale (duplicate work, fail_under enforced by ubuntu, macOS runner scarcity) is not documented — losing the intent of the deliverable.
findings.suggested_fix: Change AC#7 to: 'docs/coverage.md states that CI collects coverage on the ubuntu cells only, and explains why (coverage tracing is duplicate work on macOS given ubuntu enforces the fail_under floor, and macOS runner slots are scarce).'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` (or add a new test in it) to assert that the macOS cell's default-suite step contains neither `--cov` nor `--cov-report`, and that the ubuntu cell's default-suite step contains both `--cov=rebar` and `--cov-report=term-missing:skip-covered`.
evidence: Plan: "`tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` pins the substring `pytest -m "not integration and not external"` (line 67), which this change preserves; that suite must stay green"

AC1: 'The macOS matrix cells run the default suite with no `--cov` or `--cov-report` flags'
AC2: 'The ubuntu matrix cells still pass `--cov=rebar --cov-report=term-missing:skip-covered`'
findings.finding: The testing plan relies on `test_ci_workflow_parity.py` (line 67) staying green as the sole automated guard, but that test only pins the `-m` marker substring — it does NOT assert that macOS cells lack `--cov`/`--cov-report` flags (AC1) or that ubuntu cells retain them (AC2). The changed behavior has no corresponding test work, so the suite can be green while the flag conditionality is wrong or accidentally regresses later.
findings.location: Testing section / Acceptance Criteria AC1–AC2 / tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py
scenarios: A future workflow edit accidentally re-adds `--cov` to the macOS cell; the parity test stays green and the regression goes undetected
The conditionality logic is written incorrectly (e.g. wrong matrix key comparison) so both platforms skip coverage; the parity test still passes
findings.suggested_fix: Parse the workflow YAML in the test (using `yaml.safe_load` on `_build-and-test.yml`) and assert per-platform step `run:` contents: for the macOS matrix entry, `'--cov' not in run_cmd`; for ubuntu, `'--cov=rebar' in run_cmd` and `'--cov-report=term-missing:skip-covered' in run_cmd`.

findings.finding: The plan says 'Make the coverage flags conditional on the matrix OS' but does not specify the exact YAML mechanism — step-level `if: matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest'`, separate run: blocks, an env var branch, or an inline shell conditional — leaving the executor to choose.
